definitions.main: One highest original target-predicate softmax-probability query per GT identity pair and predicate, across all continuous segments; no GT time used. This is a fixed readout diagnostic, NOT the native multiple-query detector.
definitions.oracle: Best tIoU across all original identity-compatible queries, strict float32 sigmoid>.5 hull, min5; GT-assisted availability, NOT achieved recall.
definitions.pair_covers: The chosen query input segment covers all GT event frames; chosen class-only query may otherwise select another continuous segment.
definitions.single_episode: Exactly one annotated GT instance for this video, ordered identity pair, predicate; other predicates or unannotated events may still exist.
definitions.target: relation duration<3s and continuous GT co-presence>=10s
definitions.sampling: GT27 previously selected diagnostic validation videos, no new generalization claim
definitions.fractions: All ratios carry integer numerators and explicit denominators. Endpoint errors condition on nonempty output; no-response remains in hit denominator.

conclusions_supported: The fixed top-class single-query readout is heavily confounded by selecting another input segment and by reuse across repeated events; 758/2573 is not the native detector recall.

Within 84 long-coexisting short events with chosen input covering GT and only one annotated same-predicate episode, only 22/84 have any original query hull matching at tIoU>=.5; repeated same-predicate episodes and disjoint selected support cannot fully explain this subset.
In that subset the selected query produces a nonempty interval in 84/84, and 81/84 are longer than the GT interval. This is a measured output pattern, not proof of a context-suppression mechanism.
The endpoint-error and fixed-0.2s metric simulation describe different quantities. Simulation isolates metric sensitivity and is not a model intervention or performance claim.
conclusions_not_supported: Do not attribute all fixed-top1 errors to temporal localization: the original detector uses multiple queries and does not force one query onto all repeated GT events.
No causal evidence here distinguishes visual ambiguity, temporal encoding loss, query specialization, supervision, or historical-context suppression.
Do not claim longitudinal co-presence causes failure from these unbalanced selected slices. Use the separately controlled-duration and predicate experiment.
Do not treat outside-GT positive mask as a visually verified false relation; visual annotation remains to be checked.
Small predicate slices are descriptive, with video clustering and different cohort composition; no independent significance claim is made.
